phase3_findings.description: On the opt-in band path, search_similar_usage runs after search_text_memories has already returned; if only the band (SQL-pair) search raises, the already-fetched text memories are dropped too and the prompt degrades to unmodified. Fail-toward-no-change and warned (within the intended degrade contract), but a slight behavioral widening vs pre-change where only text search could fail. No action required unless preserving partial text-memory injection on a band-search failure is desired.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: no-fix (advisory; below verdict threshold; consistent with required degrade contract)

phase3_findings.description: Band can be starved by strict-tier crowding under the shared limit=5. search_similar_usage(limit=5) maps to Chroma n_results=5 and the score<strict exclusion is applied after retrieval, so when the 5 nearest neighbours are all strict-tier hits, band_pairs collapses to empty even though in-band pairs exist just outside the top-5. AC4 ('every saved memory in band') is thus best-effort, capped at 5. Practically benign (strict hits stay reusable via the search tool) and mirrors the pre-existing text limit=5. Consider a note or a larger band candidate set.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: no-fix (advisory; below verdict threshold; pre-existing limit=5 tradeoff, not a regression)

phase3_findings.description: Band-enabled text floor is asserted only indirectly. test_band_injects_both_memory_kinds_as_prose asserts tool_search_calls == [0.3] but not text_search_calls; a one-line assert mem.text_search_calls == [0.3] would pin text_search_floor = min(context_floor, strict) directly for the band-enabled path.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: no-fix (advisory test hardening; below verdict threshold)

phase3_findings.description: Inverted/above-strict context_similarity_threshold (e.g. 0.9/0.7) is valid input but untested. Source handles it correctly (band_enabled False; text_search_floor = min(0.9,0.7)=0.7) but no test pins that min() never lets the text floor rise above strict. Degenerate config; optional.

Degrade path test only exercises search_text_memories raising, not search_similar_usage. Both calls sit inside the same try, so the second raise is covered by symmetry; an explicit case would be belt-and-suspenders.

No cross-field validator ties context_similarity_threshold to similarity_threshold. Because both defaults are independently 0.7, a user who lowers only similarity_threshold (e.g. to 0.5) leaves context_similarity_threshold at 0.7 (>= strict), silently disabling the near-match band with no warning. Behaviour is well-defined and the enhancer degrades safely, but the relational invariant lives only in prose. Usability foot-gun, not a bug.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: no-fix (advisory; below verdict threshold; optional warning-only model_validator)

phase3_findings.description: _StubAgentMemory duplicates production's >= similarity_threshold lower-bound filtering inline in two methods. If the real ChromaAgentMemory gate ever changes, the stub keeps encoding the old behaviour and tests stay green while diverging from production. Test-fidelity/drift risk, not a correctness bug in this PR.

DefaultLlmContextEnhancer.__init__ stores similarity_threshold/context_similarity_threshold as plain public floats with no range re-validation at this layer. Acceptable because factory.build_agent feeds already-validated MemoryConfig values, but a programmatic caller constructing the enhancer directly could pass out-of-range values that bypass the [0,1] invariant.
phase3_findings.fix_decision: no-fix (advisory; below verdict threshold; invariant enforced at config boundary)
